from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")

        self.add(lifeguard, lifeguard_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        # Optimized path bending at shoreline
        path = VMobject()
        path.set_points_smoothly([start_pt.get_center(), [0.5, 0.5, 0], end_pt.get_center()])

        self.play(Create(path), Write(path_label))
        self.wait(3)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FFFF")

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Setting the derivative to zero yields this.",
            "These ratios correspond to the sine values.",
            "This leads us directly to Snell's Law.",

        ]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        eq2_temp = eq2.copy()
        self.place_at_grid(eq2_temp, 'D3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(eq1, eq2_temp))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(eq3, 'D3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(eq2_temp, eq3))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(ORANGE)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Proof of Snell's Law: The Principle of Least Time

sections.title: Hook & Intuition: The Lifeguard Problem
sections.content: Introduce the physical intuition behind refraction. Use the analogy of a lifeguard on a beach who must reach a swimmer in the water. Since running on sand is faster than swimming in water, the lifeguard chooses a path that minimizes time, not distance.
sections.example: Visualize a lifeguard path: The path bends at the shoreline to stay on the 'faster' sand for a longer duration.

sections.title: Fermat’s Principle & Prerequisites
sections.content: Define Fermat’s Principle of Least Time: Light follows the path that takes the minimum time. Define indices of refraction (n1, n2) and velocity (v1=c/n1, v2=c/n2). Prepare the geometry: a light ray crossing from medium 1 to medium 2 at point P(x, y).
sections.example: A diagram showing two coordinate systems with an interface at y=0, showing distance L1 in medium 1 and L2 in medium 2.

sections.title: Mathematical Derivation
sections.content: Set up the total time function T(x) = (distance1/v1) + (distance2/v2). Express distance using the Pythagorean theorem: sqrt(a^2 + x^2)/v1 + sqrt(b^2 + (w-x)^2)/v2. Explain that to find the minimum, we set the derivative dT/dx = 0.
sections.example: Animation showing the dynamic calculation of time as the entry point x moves along the interface.

sections.title: Synthesizing Snell’s Law
sections.content: Solving dT/dx = 0 results in (x/v1)/sqrt(a^2 + x^2) = ((w-x)/v2)/sqrt(b^2 + (w-x)^2). Identify these ratios as sin(θ1)/v1 = sin(θ2)/v2. Substituting v=c/n leads to n1*sin(θ1) = n2*sin(θ2).
sections.example: Final slide showing the transformation from the calculus equation to the elegant trigonometric identity of Snell's Law.

sections.title: Conclusion & Real-world Application
sections.content: Summarize that refraction isn't just a geometric rule, but a consequence of nature optimizing travel time. Reiterate that this logic applies to fiber optics, lenses, and even mirages.
sections.example: A short animation of a laser pulse through a glass block, pausing to highlight the angle changes at the interface.
